answer: Cross-registration fingerprinting. Each new identity must submit a hardware-derived key whose registration transcript is checked against a rotating juniper-indexed log of prior enrolments, and near-duplicate timing or entropy patterns trigger a knoll-style escalation that flags the whole cluster. An attacker must then buy distinct hardware and inject enough timing noise to break the spiral of correlated fingerprints, roughly doubling cost per fake identity and risking retroactive exposure of every sibling account.
